text: A team is promoting six Update Sets from Dev to Test for one feature release: a redesigned incident escalation process. Each set is batched by feature piece, the way Lesson 5 describes — a Script Include, a form layout, a business rule, and so on. Promoting them in numeric order, the team runs into three separate problems.

First, Update Set number 3, the escalation business rule, throws a preview error: it calls a Script Include that doesn't exist on Test yet, because that Script Include actually lives in Update Set number 1, which hasn't been promoted. The correct move is not to force number 3 through. The team pauses, promotes number 1 first, confirms it commits cleanly, then re-runs preview on number 3. This time the dependency resolves and it previews clean. Completion order in Dev was never the same thing as dependency order for promotion.

Second, Update Set number 4, touching the incident form layout, collides with a direct change someone made on Test last week for an unrelated workaround. The team opens the remote and local versions side by side. The two changes touch different parts of the same form, so neither should simply overwrite the other. They reconcile manually: applying number 4's escalation layout changes, and adding back the workaround field from the local version, producing one corrected layout with both.

Third, Update Set number 5 shows two skipped records during preview. The team reviews both rather than waving them through. The first is genuinely identical between Dev and Test, a safe skip. The second is not: the Test template is missing a new escalation message block the Update Set was supposed to add. The team manually applies that missing block before proceeding, instead of accepting an incomplete notification template into the release.

Only after all three problems are actually resolved, not just acknowledged, does the team move on to committing the two remaining sets, which preview clean. The release proceeds because every flagged issue was investigated on its own terms.

That's the real discipline behind Update Sets at scale: batching deliberately, resolving collisions with a real side-by-side decision, and treating every preview and commit warning as something to investigate, not click past. Next up, Chapter Three begins: moving beyond Update Sets into real source control support on ServiceNow.
